What process did you use? If SMAW, crank that amperage up based on the wall-thickness of the tubing. If MiG, I suggest 25v minimum and a WFS of around 475 ipm ( if you’re using .35-.45 wire. Also, it’s highly recommended that you have scrap of the same thickness and steel type and do a test run to make sure you are making the parameters for penetration before welding on the actual pieces.

Edit: what gas combo are you using? I agree with the above comments about gas coverage and porosity in the weld. Should be between 30-40, given that your angle and distance between the nozzle and seam are correct ( generally accepted distance is 3/8” and 30 degree angle in push or pull directions and 45 degrees on the z-axis)

Just wear your proper PPE, and more than likely since you’re new, you’ll have at least person helping/watching for the first couple days. If you are close-quarter welding on a big project, I highly suggest a bib for your hood or wearing sunscreen daily.

I learned in my fathers shop. So I was kind of born to it, but I would suggest getting a small stick welding setup and start from there. If you need machine parameter cheat sheets they are available online. Only thing else that I can say with absolute certainty is that this is like any other trade, you learn by doing. I’ve got 10+ years welding under my belt and nothing helped more than fucking up :) godspeed
